assessment.nobel_worthiness: GLP-1 physiology led to incretin-based drugs that transformed treatment of type 2 diabetes and obesity, with cardiovascular and renal benefit signals. Clear, original, and of very large clinical and societal impact.
assessment.attribution: The decisive physiology and peptide work is spread across Drucker, Holst and Mojsov (identification and characterization of the active GLP-1 form and its biology), while Knudsen is central to the drug development. The credited list omits other pioneers I recall (e.g. Habener), so the three-person configuration is imperfect.
assessment.maturity: Multiple independent, large randomized trials and wide clinical use; the interpretation is stable and recognition is timely, arguably pressing.
uncertainties: Credit among basic discoverers versus drug developers is contested and I am not certain about priority details.
A fair three-person split leaves out at least one major contributor.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optogenetics gave a general method to control defined cell types with light and reshaped neuroscience, from circuit mapping to disease models and early clinical translation (vision restoration). Original and widely used in my own field's methods, but I weigh it by common criteria.
assessment.attribution: Channelrhodopsin characterization (Nagel, Hegemann, Bamberg) and its deployment in neurons (Deisseroth, Boyden, with Miesenböck's earlier genetic photostimulation) are separable contributions. Three names cannot cover all of them fairly.
assessment.maturity: Over two decades of independent confirmation and ubiquitous use; mature. Clinical impact is still emerging, so the case rests on the tool.
uncertainties: Allocation among Boyden, Deisseroth, Miesenböck, Bamberg, Nagel and Hegemann is genuinely disputed.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Engineered CAR-T cells produced durable remissions in refractory B-cell malignancies and created a new class of cell therapy. Highly original and clinically transformative.
assessment.attribution: Sadelain and June developed and translated CAR designs with costimulation and clinical proof; Rosenberg pioneered adoptive cell therapy and early gene-engineered T cell trials. Other early CAR concept contributors (e.g. Eshhar) are not on the supplied list.
assessment.maturity: Approved products and long follow-up data support maturity; toxicity, access and solid-tumor limits remain.
uncertainties: Credit for the original chimeric receptor concept is not captured by the credited names.
Role of Rosenberg relative to the CAR designers is uncertain.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Targeting BCR-ABL with imatinib turned CML from a fatal into a chronic disease and validated molecularly targeted cancer therapy, a clear paradigm with lasting impact.
assessment.attribution: Lydon (compound development), Druker (preclinical and clinical proof) and Sawyers (resistance mechanisms and next-generation inhibitors) form a coherent trio. Foundational BCR-ABL discoveries by others are outside this candidate.
assessment.maturity: Fully mature with decades of survival data; recognition is arguably late but not premature.
uncertainties: Whether the committee views this as drug development rather than discovery, and prior recognition of the foundational biology, may reduce priority.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Antisense modulation of SMN2 splicing yielded nusinersen, the first effective therapy for spinal muscular atrophy, a strong mechanism-to-medicine story that opened antisense splicing therapeutics.
assessment.attribution: Krainer's splicing mechanism and Bennett's oligonucleotide chemistry and development fit a clean two-person credit; other contributors (e.g. Hua, Singh) are not credited and I cannot judge their weight.
assessment.maturity: Approved since 2016 with robust clinical benefit; a relatively recent but stable achievement, so timing is reasonable if somewhat early.
uncertainties: Long-term outcomes and the breadth of the platform are still being established.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: cGAS-STING defined the cytosolic DNA-sensing pathway of innate immunity with broad relevance to infection, autoimmunity, interferonopathies and cancer immunity. A conceptually clear, original discovery.
assessment.attribution: Chen identified cGAS and the second messenger cGAMP; Barber and Ishikawa identified STING. Wu and Sun worked in Chen's laboratory, so a fair prize would likely be centered on Chen and Barber, with the third slot uncertain.
assessment.maturity: Mechanism is well confirmed by many groups; therapeutic translation is still early and unproven, which makes the recognition somewhat premature in clinical terms.
uncertainties: Therapeutic impact is not yet shown.
Allocation of the third place between Ishikawa and the Chen laboratory members is unresolved.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Adult stem-cell-derived organoids from Lgr5+ cells created an enduring in vitro platform for tissue biology, disease modeling and personalized medicine. Original and broadly adopted.
assessment.attribution: Clevers led the Lgr5 stem cell and organoid work, with Sato as the first author of the key intestinal organoid papers; two-person credit is plausible. Other organoid contributors are not listed here.
assessment.maturity: Widely reproduced and extended across organs; clinical utility is still developing, but as a research platform it is mature.
uncertainties: Whether platform technology and its translational value suffice is uncertain.
Relation to other stem-cell and organoid work is not assessed from the supplied data.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Long-term potentiation is the leading cellular model of synaptic plasticity underlying learning and memory, with decades of influence. Foundational, though its in vivo link to memory remains incomplete.
assessment.attribution: Bliss and Lømo reported LTP in 1973; Collingridge showed NMDA receptor dependence, and Morris linked it to spatial learning. Three names omit one of these, a real attribution tension.
assessment.maturity: Very mature and independently replicated; the older discovery is long overdue if recognized at all, though the causal link to memory is still debated.
uncertainties: Choice among Collingridge and Morris for the third place is arguable.
Direct evidence linking LTP to memory storage remains debated.
